description: Solve data analytics problems and solutions by mastering data quality assurance. Learn why bad data happens and how to fix it on your Mac today.
intro: Data quality assurance is the most persistent challenge for data analysts. You spend your day finding, cleaning, and organizing data instead of extracting insights.
tldr: Data analysts spend 50 to 80 percent of their time on data preparation.
Poor data quality costs organizations up to 15 million dollars annually.
The 1-10-100 rule shows that fixing data early is 100 times cheaper than fixing it later.
You can improve quality with automated tests, data observability, and clear data contracts.
Lazur helps you stay focused by answering questions and guiding you through complex workflows.

stats.label: Annual cost of poor data quality

blocks.text: The hidden cost of bad data

Data analytics problems and solutions often center on the quality of your source material. When your data is dirty, your analysis is wrong. You might spend hours building a model only to realize the underlying data had duplicate entries or missing values.

The financial impact is heavy. Beyond the wasted hours, poor data leads to bad business decisions. If your report shows a false trend, your team might invest in the wrong product. This costs companies 15 to 25 percent of their revenue.

Most data quality issues stem from manual entry or broken pipelines. When humans type data into a form, they make mistakes. When systems do not talk to each other, you get silos. A change in an upstream system can break your downstream reports without notice.

You do not need an expensive enterprise suite to start. Focus on observability and testing. If you use Python or SQL, write tests that check for nulls or duplicates before your data lands in a dashboard.
Use the 1-10-100 rule. It costs 1 dollar to prevent an error, 10 dollars to fix it once found, and 100 dollars to fix it after it impacts a business process.
blocks.title: Think ahead

blocks.text: Establish data contracts. If you rely on a specific column from another team, document it. If they change the schema, the contract alerts you immediately. This prevents the classic fire-fighting mode where you scramble to fix broken reports.

faq.question: How much time do analysts spend on data cleaning?
faq.answer: Most data professionals spend 50 to 80 percent of their time preparing and cleaning data.

faq.question: What is the 1-10-100 rule?
faq.answer: It is a framework suggesting that preventing a data error is 1 dollar, fixing it once found is 10 dollars, and fixing it after it impacts business is 100 dollars.

faq.question: Is it better to use tools or write custom scripts?
faq.answer: For smaller tasks, custom Python or SQL scripts work well. For complex data pipelines, use observability tools like Great Expectations or dbt tests.

causes.title: Manual processes
causes.text: Human error during data entry creates inconsistencies that are hard to track.

causes.title: System silos
causes.text: When systems do not share definitions, you end up with duplicate or conflicting records.

causes.title: Lack of governance
causes.text: Without clear rules on data ownership, small errors grow into massive problems.

fixes.title: Automated testing
fixes.text: Write scripts to check for null values or duplicates automatically.

fixes.title: Data contracts
fixes.text: Agree with data producers on the format of incoming data to avoid surprises.

fixes.title: Data observability
fixes.text: Monitor your pipelines in real time to catch anomalies before they reach reports.
